target_customer: Small and medium sellers in Nigeria and wider Africa who sell through chat, and the buyers who pay them
problem: Informal sellers take orders and payments by chat and manage inventory, invoices and payment confirmation by hand. Buyers do not want to download an app or sign up to buy.
business_model: SaaS subscription plans for merchants (a Business Plus plan is referenced) plus payment processing fees
product_category: WhatsApp storefronts and chat payments, later described as agentic payments infrastructure

founders.name: Kayode Disu
founders.background_notes: YC page says over 15 years building digital security and payment solutions for banks and payment switches in West Africa. Employers and education not stated.

founders.name: Peter Ekunkoya
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in a search summary of a YesPress profile and a VC4A profile; I could not open those pages, and the YC page lists only Disu.

competitors.name: Flutterwave Store
competitors.what: Free storefront for African SMEs attached to Flutterwave payments, shareable by link on social media
competitors.traction_then: Live and documented in 2021 how-to coverage
competitors.funding_then: Flutterwave was a well funded payments company; no figure checked

competitors.name: Paystack Commerce
competitors.what: Social commerce storefront product from Paystack launched June 2020
competitors.funding_then: Paystack was owned by Stripe by 2020; not checked in sources opened

technical_complexity.rationale: Building on the WhatsApp Business API with order, invoice and payment flows is standard engineering, but licensing as a payment provider and PCI compliance add real work.

defensibility.rationale: Storefront features are copyable, and big gateways already offered storefronts. The company later cites a CBN payment licence and Meta provider status as differentiators.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Gateways offered competing storefronts from 2020. By December 2024 Paystack partnered with Vendy rather than replacing it, per press coverage.

market_need_then: BusinessDay reports that a large share of online purchases in Nigeria start with a chat, and sellers relied on WhatsApp and Instagram for sales in 2020 to 2022.

branding.domain_note: Operates on myvendy.com, not vendy.com; no acquisition history found.

identity.visual_style: Clean SaaS marketing site with partner and compliance logos
identity.voice_and_tone: Simple and conversational, tagline about making payment as simple as a chat

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand itself found. The site leans on Meta, Stripe and YC logos rather than a distinctive identity.

pivots.from: Marketplace on WhatsApp with customized shops
pivots.to: Agentic payments infrastructure for social platforms and AI chatbots
pivots.why: Positioning on the current website; no date or reason stated.

outcome_analysis: Vendy is still operating as of the latest sources. It added licences and partnerships such as Paystack in December 2024 and Kuda, and moved its positioning toward payments infrastructure. Funding is not verified beyond aggregator figures, so the scale of its raise is unknown, and competing gateway storefronts predate it.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators (a YesPress profile and one directory) report a March 2022 round of either about 1.2M or 500K USD with YC, Ventures Platform and Voltron Capital, and another aggregator reports 3.7M over 3 rounds; none was confirmed by a press release or company source, so no round is recorded. TechCabal pages returned 403. CB Insights gives a 2021 founding year. Bumpa raised a 4M seed in October 2022, after the batch, so it is not listed.
